itens.titulo: AMD to report Q3 results following disappointing showing from Intel
itens.descricao: AMD to report Q3 results following disappointing showing from Intel Yahoo Finance
trechos: Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 earnings after the bell Thursday, but provided Q4 revenue estimates of between $15 billion and $16 billion, well below analysts' projections of $17 billion.
The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29%.
For the third quarter, analysts anticipate AMD to report earnings per share of $1.97 on revenue of $13 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.
AMD's Data Center arm is expected to see sales of $8.19 billion, an 88% increase from the $4.34 billion it reported last year.
The company's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, is set to top $3.06 billion, up 11% year over year, but flat sequentially.
AMD's gaming business, however, could take a major hit, with Wall Street predicting a 49% revenue decline to $655 million.

itens.titulo: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking AI tech deal, both stocks tank
itens.descricao: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking AI tech deal, both stocks tank Yahoo Finance
trechos: What happened: Marvell Technology (MRVL) shares fell more than 10% on Monday after the chip designer announced it will acquire optical component maker Lumentum (LITE) in a deal valued at $115 billion.
Lumentum shares also fell 15% following the announcement.
Under the agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each share owned.
While that exchange ratio initially implied a valuation of $1,132 per share based on Oct.
28 prices, Marvell's recent drop has steadily eroded the payout's actual value.
The record-breaking agreement is expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, according to the announcement.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Matt Murphy, chairman and CEO of Marvell, said on Monday.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company." The company joined the S&P 500 (^GSPC) index in June.

itens.titulo: Options traders are getting anxious on Palantir and Apple ahead of earnings
itens.descricao: Options traders are getting anxious on Palantir and Apple ahead of earnings CNBC
trechos: The two stocks have been on trajectories that are distinct from the broader AI trade – with Apple, in particular, trading almost inversely to the Nasdaq 100 Index – but that's not stopping speculators from betting on a reversal in their shares after earnings.
Of the 620,000 options traded on Apple by midday, 385,000 were puts, with at least 113,000 puts likely initiated by buyers, compared to just 64,000 calls bought, Cboe LiveVol data show.
At the same time, the price of puts reached the 86th percentile of the past year, compared to the 51st percentile for calls, according to data from Nations Indexes.
Apple stock is up 25% this year and currently trading with a negative 0.65 correlation with the Nasdaq 100, ThinkOrSwim data show.
Options are implying just under a 4% move for the stock, compared to the average 2.5% swing after earnings the past two years, according to LiveVol.
Palantir options flows are also leaning bearish, with more puts trading than calls by volume and the price of puts at the 97th percentile of the past year, according to Nations Indexes.
Calls are pricey, too, but not as much – they're in the 76th percentile.
Traders should be ready for a big move in Palantir: market-makers are pricing an 11.5% implied move, compared to the 10% average the past two years.

itens.titulo: ETFs to Watch as Amazon Shares Slip Following Q3 Earnings Miss
itens.descricao: ETFs to Watch as Amazon Shares Slip Following Q3 Earnings Miss Yahoo Finance Australia
trechos: Shares of Amazon.com AMZN slipped 1.4% in the last trading session, recovering from a plunge of more than 6% in after-hours trading on Oct.
29, following the release of its third-quarter results.
The tech giant's rising free cash outflow marred the AWS unit's fastest sales growth of 39.3% in nearly five years, a tension directly reflected in the stock's volatility.
A Brief Analysis of AMZN's Q3 Results Amazon's third-quarter earnings of $1.89 missed the consensus estimate by 6%.
On a year-over-year basis, the company's earnings dropped 3.1%, while its sales grew 12%.
The company's advertising business delivered solid growth in the third quarter, with revenues increasing 12% year over year.

Its grocery business is also delivering solid growth, with fresh groceries and everyday essentials growing about 3x faster than the rest of the store and representing about half of all units sold in the third quarter.

As customers continue migrating to the cloud and expanding their use of Amazon Web Services ("AWS") core offerings, the segment's annualized revenue run rate reached $184 billion at the end of the third quarter.
